arxiv-2107-08976.title: OODformer: Out-Of-Distribution Detection Transformer
arxiv-2107-08976.creator: Rajat Koner, Poulami Sinhamahapatra, Karsten Roscher, Stephan Günnemann, Volker Tresp
arxiv-2107-08976.description: Abstract A serious problem in image classification is that a trained model might perform well for input data that originates from the same distribution as the data available for model training, but performs much worse for out-of-distribution (OOD) samples. In real-world safety-critical applications, in particular, it is important to be aware if a new data point is OOD.

arxiv-2303-05995.title: Exploring Gender Bias in Remote Pair Programming among Software Engineering Students: The twincode Original Study and First External Replication Manuscript under review in Empirical Software Engineering
arxiv-2303-05995.creator: Amador Durán, Pablo Fernández, Beatriz Bernárdez, Nathaniel Weinman, Aslıhan Akalın, Armando Fox
arxiv-2303-05995.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Amador Durán, Pablo Fernández, Beatriz Bernárdez, Nathaniel Weinman, Aslıhan Akalın, Armando Fox. Women have historically been underrepresented in Software Engineering, due in part to an unwelcoming climate pervaded by the widely-held gender bias that men outperform women at programming. Pair programming is both widely used in industry and has been shown to increase student interest in Software Engineering, particularly among women; but if those same gender biases are also present in pair programming, its potential for attracting women to the field could be thwarted.

arxiv-2304-13766.title: Preserving Superconvergence of Spectral Elements for Curved Domains via h h and p p -Geometric Refinement
arxiv-2304-13766.creator: Jacob Jones, Rebecca Conley, Xiangmin Jiao
arxiv-2304-13766.description: Abstract Spectral element methods (SEM), which are extensions of finite element methods (FEM), are important emerging techniques for solving partial differential equations in physics and engineering. SEM can potentially deliver better accuracy due to the potential superconvergence for well-shaped tensor-product elements.

arxiv-2311-02748.title: Pyclipse , a library for deidentification of free-text clinical notes
arxiv-2311-02748.creator: Callandra Moore \ORCID 0009-0008-3801-3137, Jonathan Ranisau \ORCID 0000-0002-1178-7510, Walter Nelson \ORCID 0000-0002-5216-7617, Jeremy Petch \ORCID 0000-0003-1614-1046, Alistair Johnson \ORCID 0000-0002-8735-3014
arxiv-2311-02748.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Callandra Moore \ORCID 0009-0008-3801-3137, Jonathan Ranisau \ORCID 0000-0002-1178-7510, Walter Nelson \ORCID 0000-0002-5216-7617, Jeremy Petch \ORCID 0000-0003-1614-1046, Alistair Johnson \ORCID 0000-0002-8735-3014. Automated deidentification of clinical text data is crucial due to the high cost of manual deidentification, which has been a barrier to sharing clinical text and the advancement of clinical natural language processing. However, creating effective automated deidentification tools faces several challenges, including issues in reproducibility due to differences in text processing, evaluation methods, and a lack of consistency across clinical domains and institutions.

arxiv-2311-03040.title: Grouping Local Process Models
arxiv-2311-03040.creator: Viki Peeva, Wil M.P. van der Aalst
arxiv-2311-03040.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Viki Peeva, Wil M.P. van der Aalst. In recent years, process mining emerged as a proven technology to analyze and improve operational processes. An expanding range of organizations using process mining in their daily operation brings a broader spectrum of processes to be analyzed. Some of these processes are highly unstructured, making it difficult for traditional process discovery approaches to discover a start-to-end model describing the entire process.

arxiv-2501-19253.creator: Eduard Looijenga
arxiv-2501-19253.description: Abstract . Classical Hodge theory endows the square integrable cohomology of a Shimura variety X X with values in a locally homogeneous polarized variation of Hodge structure 𝔼 {\mathbb{E}} with a natural Hodge decomposition. pmc-10507073.title: Predicting unplanned readmissions in the intensive care unit: a multimodality evaluation
pmc-10507073.creator: Eitam Sheetrit, Menachem Brief, Oren Elisha
pmc-10507073.description: A hospital readmission is when a patient who was discharged from the hospital is admitted again for the same or related care within a certain period. Hospital readmissions are a significant problem in the healthcare domain, as they lead to increased hospitalization costs, decreased patient satisfaction, and increased risk of adverse outcomes such as infections, medication errors, and even death.

pmc-11349757.title: Temporal trends and long-term outcomes of radiofrequency ablation for hepatocellular carcinoma within the Milan criteria
pmc-11349757.creator: Se Young Jang, Soo Young Park, Young Oh Kweon, Yu Rim Lee, Hun Kyu Ryeom, Jung Guen Cha, Sungmin Kim, Won Kee Lee, Ae Jeong Jo, Won Young Tak
pmc-11349757.description: No study has analysed the temporal trends of the long-term results and clinical characteristics of patients with hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) treated using radiofrequency ablation (RFA). Therefore, we examined temporal trends of characteristics of patients and treatment-naïve HCCs within the Milan criteria treated by RFA over 20 years.

pmc-11433238.title: Non-Zoonotic Transmission of Sporotrichosis: A Translational Study of Forty-Three Cases in a Zoonotic Hyperendemic Area
pmc-11433238.creator: Juliana Nahal, Rowena Alves Coelho, Fernando Almeida-Silva, Andréa Reis Bernardes-Engemann, Anna Carolina Procópio-Azevedo, Vanessa Brito de Souza Rabello, Rayanne Gonçalves Loureiro, Dayvison Francis Saraiva Freitas, Antonio Carlos Francesconi do Valle, Priscila Marques de Macedo, Manoel Marques Ev
pmc-11433238.description: Over the past two decades, zoonotic sporotrichosis transmitted by naturally infected cats has become hyperendemic in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil. Sporothrix brasiliensis is the main agent involved. However, there are other forms of transmission of sporotrichosis. The aim of this study was to evaluate and associate the epidemiological, clinical and therapeutic data and the susceptibility of Sporothrix spp.

pmc-11623866.title: Unraveling the role of PBK in glioblastoma: from molecular mechanisms to therapeutic targets
pmc-11623866.creator: Yizheng Zhang, Mingyuan Luan
pmc-11623866.description: Background:This study investigates the gene expression characteristics of glioma-initiating cells (GIC), an important subgroup of glioblastoma (GBM), after knockdown of PBK (PDZ-binding kinase). Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) between PBK knockdown GIC and control groups were screened through bioinformatics methods. The authors analyzed the mechanisms and roles of these DEGs in GBM tumorigenesis and patient prognosis.

pmc-13056897.title: Reliable parameter estimation of nonlinear chaotic systems and PMSMs with the stellar oscillation optimizer
pmc-13056897.creator: Serdar Ekinci, Davut Izci, Mostafa Jabari, Fahmi Elsayed, Mohammad Salman, Burcu Bektaş Güneş
pmc-13056897.description: Accurate parameter identification is a critical prerequisite for reliable modeling, analysis, and control of nonlinear dynamical systems. This study introduces the stellar oscillation optimizer (SOO), a recently proposed metaheuristic inspired by the oscillatory behavior of stars, and investigates its effectiveness in estimating system parameters through a unified optimization framework.

pmc-13247116.title: Exploring the Mechanisms of Total Saponins of Black Ginseng and Ginsenoside Rg3 Against Doxorubicin‐Induced Cardiotoxicity
pmc-13247116.creator: Linlin Liu, Peiyuan Dou, Xiaotong Zhang, Xiaoku Ran, Deqiang Dou, Xiaodong Lv
pmc-13247116.description: Doxorubicin (DOX), a widely utilized chemotherapeutic agent, is constrained by its intricate cardiotoxicity, which involves oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and cell death. Black ginseng (BG), processed to enhance rare saponins such as ginsenoside Rg3, demonstrates augmented anticancer and cardioprotective properties.

pmc-13346923.title: Application of Pseudomonas mosselii PR5 Enables Fertilizer Reduction in Rice While Maintaining Yield, Grain Quality, and Soil Nutrient Dynamics
pmc-13346923.creator: Sourav Biswas Shuvo, Razia Sultana, Shah Mohammad Naimul Islam, Imam Mehedi, Md. Azmain Farek Milon
pmc-13346923.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). The use of inorganic fertilizers in rice farming has led to increased production costs, reduced nutritional value, and it results in major ecological damage. Harnessing plant growth‐promoting rhizobacteria (PGPR) offers a promising eco‐friendly alternative to conventional fertilization strategies. This study evaluates the potential of Pseudomonas mosselii PR5 as a bioinoculant to enhance rice growth under reduced fertilizer inputs in a pot experiment.

pmc-13486290.description: BackgroundValid measures of behavioral health access and social determinants of health (SDOH) can inform health promotion, programming, and strategies to address identified gaps.
